Asset overview
58
Drug candidate
BI 3802876 is a bispecific molecule binding FAP and TRAILR2.
Clinical hypothesis
Selectively removing FAP+ TRAILR2+ activated Hepatic Stellate Cells will halt/reverse liver fibrosis
Unique MOA
Directly targeting the source of liver fibrosis
FAP binding provides cell specificity and clusters TRAILR2 mediates cell killing
Indication
NASH cF4 is a sentinel population with the potential to expand to other etiologies as a Pan-Cirrhotic Therapy
Treatment paradigm
Intravenous drug, monthly or longer
Short term/Cycling/Induction therapy
Competition
No direct clinical competition for MoA in MASH
Pre-clinical results
Demonstrated anti-fibrotic PoC in LiverChip (in vitro) fibrosis model with clinically relevant biomarkers (see next slide)
Phase I results
BI 3802876 may cause small increases in hs-cTnT, which are of uncertain clinical significance at this time.

Drug candidate
BI 3802876 is a bispecific molecule binding FAP and TRAILR2.
Clinical hypothesis
Selectively removing FAP+ TRAILR2+ activated Hepatic Stellate Cells will halt/reverse liver fibrosis
Unique MOA
Directly targeting the source of liver fibrosis
FAP binding provides cell specificity and clusters TRAILR2 mediates cell killing
Indication
MASH cF4 is a sentinel population with the potential to expand to other etiologies as a Pan-Cirrhotic Therapy
Treatment paradigm
Intravenous drug, monthly or longer
Short term/Cycling/Induction therapy
Competition
No direct clinical competition for MoA in MASH
Pre-clinical results
Demonstrated anti-fibrotic PoC in LiverChip (in vitro) fibrosis model with clinically relevant biomarkers (see next slide)
Phase I results
BI 3802876 may cause small increases in hs-cTnT, which are of uncertain clinical significance at this time.

Executive Summary

SGLT2i significantly reduce cardiovascular and renal events in CKD patients, leading to their inclusion as first-line therapy in both global (KDIGO 2024) and Chinese (2023/2025) guidelines.

Study background
The cardiovascular and kidney benefits of SGLT2 inhibitors in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are well established in large pivotal trials. This has prompted updates to SGLT2 inhibitor drug licences and the publication/update of clinical guidelines relating to their use, including ‘Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes’ (KDIGO) guidelines in 2024 and ‘Guidelines for the early evaluation and management of chronic kidney disease in China’ in 2023.
However, the implementation of updated SGLT2 inhibitor guidelines and prescribing in the real-world CKD population remains largely unknown
Understanding treatment opportunity gaps, highlighting potential barriers and disparities are essential in guiding the successful GDMT.
Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO). Kidney Int 2024;105:S117.
ONLY FOR INTERNAL USE

The Gap Between SGLT2i Guideline Recommendations and Real-World Practice in CKD Management Highlights the Urgent Need for Real-World Research
Established Cardiorenal Benefits of SGLT2i
Large clinical trials have demonstrated that SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) significantly reduce cardiovascular and renal events in CKD patients, leading to their inclusion as first-line therapy in both global (KDIGO 2024) and Chinese (2023/2025) guidelines.
Discrepancy Between Guidelines and Clinical Practice
Despite strong recommendations, the real-world prescription rate, treatment patterns, and influencing factors for SGLT2i use among CKD patients in China remain unclear. There is a lack of systematic, nationwide data, which hinders effective guideline implementation and maximization of patient benefit.
Rationale for the Study
There is an urgent need for real-world studies to systematically assess SGLT2i use, guideline adherence, and barriers in CKD management in China.
Understanding treatment opportunity gaps, highlighting potential barriers and disparities are essential in guiding the successful GDMT,  optimize CKD management strategies and improve patient outcomes.

Unique Value of Real-World Data
Real-world studies (RWS) can leverage multiple data sources (e.g., CDC surveillance, EHR, insurance claims) to systematically reveal prevalence, treatment patterns and  outcomes.
RWD provides localized baseline data and clinical practice context for phase III studies, supporting a comprehensive understanding of the value of innovative therapies in real-world settings.
Existing literature and guidelines highlight the need for further studies on real-world management and outcomes in this population.

RWS Provides Critical Complement to Phase III Trials, Supporting Optimized Future Chronic Disease Management in China
Closing data gap through revealing the treatment landscape of high-risk multimorbidity populations in China
Complement RCT evidence, enhancing external validity and supporting localized interpretation of results
RWS provide local data on patient characteristics, medication use, adherence, and outcomes, supporting interpretation and application of EASi™-PROTKT phase III results in China.
Inform clinical and policy decisions:
Systematic evaluation of prevalence, treatment patterns and outcomes helps identify practice gaps and supports guideline updates and policy making.
RWS evidence supports innovation in chronic disease management, tiered care, and multidisciplinary collaboration, as emphasized by both domestic and international guidelines.

text:
Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a persistent autoimmune rheumatic disorder affecting multiple organs, with significant unmet needs in therapeutic options.
The pathogenesis of SSc is characterized by a complex interplay of vasculopathy, immune dysregulation and progressive fibrosis1–4
SSc is clinically heterogeneous and can affect the skin and several internal organs1,4,5
ILD is the most common and the leading cause of mortality among complications in patients with SSc. Globally, the prevalence of ILD in SSc patients is 50%-80%6.

text:
Preclinical evidence on Nerandomilast in SSc
CONFIDENTIAL ONLY FOR INTERNAL USE
Pre-clinical data demonstrate that nerandomilast targets key pathogenic mechanisms of SSc — fibrosis, vasculopathy, and immune dysregulation — across relevant in vitro and in vivo models, with effects observed at clinically relevant concentrations. Importantly, these effects were not limited to the lung but also included skin and vascular tissues, supporting its potential for systemic disease modification.
Pre-clinical data show direct anti-fibrotic effects on lung and SSc skin fibroblasts and suppression of epithelial cell and keratinocyte pro-fibrotic activation
Potential to directly impact endothelial activation (literature and emerging in-house data) and indirectly through suppression of inflammation
Potential to directly attenuate skin fibrosis by inhibiting pro-fibrotic activation of keratinocytes and promoting barrier function
Potential to directly attenuate inflammation by modulating macrophage and lymphocyte activation and suppression of pro-inflammatory cytokines and IFNs (activities on macrophages are differentiated from MMF)

text:
Evidence from subgroup analyses in patients with SSc-ILD (trial 1305-0023)
CONFIDENTIAL ONLY FOR INTERNAL USE
The analysis of primary and key secondary endpoints in a subgroup of patients with SSc-ILD, though based on a relatively small sample size (n=75), provides compelling evidence supporting the potential efficacy of nerandomilast in this patient population.
In the SSc-ILD subgroup, nerandomilast showed numerically favorable trends in both primary and key secondary endpoints, despite the limited sample size. Safety data in this subgroup were generally consistent with the overall safety profile.
These findings support the clinical relevance of the pre-clinical data and justify further evaluation of nerandomilast on ILD and other organ manifestations in SSc in a confirmatory Phase III trial.

text:
Summary
CONFIDENTIAL ONLY FOR INTERNAL USE
The combined non-clinical and clinical data provide a strong scientific rationale to initiate a Phase III trial of nerandomilast in SSc.
Pre-clinical data demonstrate that nerandomilast targets key pathogenic mechanisms of SSc — fibrosis, vasculopathy, and immune dysregulation — across relevant in vitro and in vivo models, with effects observed at clinically relevant concentrations. Importantly, these effects were not limited to the lung but also included skin and vascular tissues, supporting its potential for systemic disease modification.
Clinically, nerandomilast has demonstrated consistent efficacy and safety in two large Phase III trials in fibrosing ILDs (IPF and PPF). In the SSc-ILD subgroup, nerandomilast showed numerically favourable trends in both primary and key secondary endpoints, despite the limited sample size. Safety data in this subgroup were consistent with the overall safety profile.
These findings support the clinical relevance of the pre-clinical data and justify further evaluation of nerandomilast on ILD and other organ manifestations in SSc in a confirmatory Phase III trial.

Overview of Feedback Received from FDA, CDE, and PMDA Following the Pre-CTA HAI
17
Proceed directly into a Ph3 in SSc without conducting a dedicated ph2
Overall study design to support target indication of “treatment of SSc” (study population, endpoints, statistical analysis strategy, safety, dose regimen)
FDA: The SSc-ILD subgroup data’s relevance to the broader SSc population remains uncertain; a ph 2 dose-finding/POC trial is recommended to guide ph3; conducting a ph3 trial based on available data is at your discretion.
CDE: current evidence is insufficient to justify proceeding directly to a pivotal trial for SSc; a dose-exploratory trial for SSc or provide additional evidence would support advancing to a pivotal trial for SSc.
PMDA: trial cannot be considered a confirmatory study due to insufficient evidence.
FDA: No regulatory precedent exists regarding primary endpoint; efficacy must show improvement across multiple core components; variability in assessment and interpretation (e.g. mRSS) should be considered; dose reduction impact on efficacy and safety need to be considered; data from the planned ph 3 study in the SSc-ILD subgroup may support an independent SSc-ILD indication.
CDE: /.
PMDA: Interpreting the results may be difficult, and there is a high risk that a negative judgment may have to be made even if proposed primary endpoint meets; no intention to halt the conduct of the 1305-0052 trial due to no safety concerns; even if a pre-NDA consultation is conducted based on the trial’s findings, there is concern that it may not result in NDA approval.
RoFD in SSc has been released by BUEC on Nov 18th , and ph3 in SSc will be proceeded as planned.

Team proposal: submit China CTA after FDA feedback on US CTA.
    - Pros: New IND released by FDA may support China CTA/EC arguments.

text:
Topic: BI 3802876 (FAP/TRAILR2) Asian Phase 1 in MASH Cirrhosis – China HA Interaction Strategy & Joint Asian Phase 1 Plan (PEC Endorsement Request)
background: CV safety findings (hs-cTnT increases of uncertain clinical significance) were identified in studies 1517-0001 SRD Part A and MD Part B in healthy volunteers. Global has initiated Phase 2a (1517-0002) in MASH cirrhosis patients to establish positive benefit/risk before PoC trial. There is uncertainty about China and Japan requiring Asian data before integrating into the next global phase trial. Global confirmed budget for Asian Phase 1 was secured.；BI 3802876 may cause small increases in hs-cTnT of uncertain clinical significance; data from other TRAILR2 agonists suggests hepatotoxicity as a potential risk; absence of Asian data; TDO not available.；Other TRAILR2 agonists suggest hepatotoxicity as a potential associated risk.；Absence of Asian data is identified as a key factor in the PK backloading assessment.；TDO not available, relevant to exposure in patient assessment.；Asian Phase 1 design: open-label, two dose groups, single dose, MASH cirrhosis population (same as global Phase 2a). 9 patients total: Japan 3+3 pts in DG1&DG2; China skips DG1, 3 pts in DG2. Dose Escalation Committee after 30-day safety observation in DG1.；Three scenarios for global and Asian timelines: Scenario 1 – both PMDA and CDE request Asian data before Phase 2b (joint Asian Phase 1, FSS~LSO 2027/Mar~2027/Oct); Scenario 2 – PMDA requests Asian data, CDE agrees to PK backloading (China remains in Asian Phase 1 for early data, potential waiver of extensive PK study); Scenario 3 – only CDE requests Asian data (China alone Phase 1, FSS~LSO 2027/Jun~2028/Feb, 4 months behind joint Asian Phase 1).；Scenario 3 (China alone Phase 1): completion is 4 months behind joint Asian Phase 1, delaying Chinese enrollment in Phase 2b. Mitigation: include preliminary Phase 1 data at time of CTA submission.；Risk 1: CDE may not agree with limited patient number in Asian Phase 1, particularly DG1 (n=3). Mitigation: emphasize trial is not first-in-human but bridges Asian and Caucasian data; present global data. Risk 2: internal competition of three MASH cirrhosis trials may impact enrollment. Mitigation: prevent overlap in site selection.；China not joining DG1 due to very limited window; need to provide strong rationale why only 3 pts for DG1.；China will submit CTA in parallel with global; snapshot of DG2 safety data to be included in CTA submission.

Topic: ECR研究概念（HTN+T2D+eCVD无HF患者患病率、治疗模式与结局）PEC及CEC背书请求
background: 主要目标：评估中国HTN+T2D+eCVD（无HF）患者的临床结局（CV死亡、HHF或紧急HF就诊）；次要目标：描述治疗模式、估计患病率。；研究设计：基于北京医保数据、病案首页、死因监测数据及CCDRFS的回顾性观察研究（ECR），咨询CDC临床专家。主要队列识别期：2019年1月1日至2024年12月31日，随访至2027年12月31日；横断面识别期及探索性终点队列另有安排。；研究背景与战略价值：中国HTN+T2D+eCVD共病患者数量庞大且持续增长，极高风险发展为HF；EASi™-PROTKT III期试验进行中，预计2030年4月出结果；利用RWD提供本地证据，支持HF Tier 1预防策略及终点估算参考数据，指导医学策略、HCP教育及未来指南。；总预算225万元人民币。关键里程碑：2025年12月CEC&PEC背书，2026年4月公司背书，2026年7月CTP申请，2026年12月合同签署，2028年12月最终分析，2029年3月CTR，2029年12月手稿，2029年8月ESC大会，2030年1月DBL，2031年4月中国申报。

Topic: Nerandomilast SSc适应症中国开发策略（研究1305-0052）
background: 全球策略：基于FIBRONEER-ILD试验SSc-ILD亚组数据及支持性临床前证据，不等待ph2b CONQUEST试验结果，直接推进SSc适应症ph3试验。；中国整合策略已于2025年8月获CEC背书。；FDA、CDE和PMDA的Pre-CTA HAI反馈一致指出现有数据不足以支持SSc确证性ph3试验，并提出最终NDA批准风险。；BUEC于2025年11月18日发布SSc的RoFD，SSc ph3试验将按计划推进。；中国CTA潜在风险：CDE尚未就具体研究设计提供反馈，CTA审评期间可能附带证据不足相关备注；EC可能因SSc患者风险获益不明确提出顾虑；NDA批准SSc适应症存在挑战。；中国CTA提交策略（FDA反馈后提交）已于11月获CEC背书，并与全球ET对齐；NDA批准风险已于11月告知本地AT。；FDA反馈：SSc-ILD亚组数据对更广泛SSc人群的相关性不确定，建议开展ph2剂量探索/POC试验；基于现有数据推进ph3由申办方自行决定。；CDE反馈：现有证据不足以直接推进SSc确证性试验，需开展剂量探索试验或提供额外证据。；PMDA反馈：因证据不足，该试验不能被视为确证性研究；即使主要终点达到，也存在被否定判断的高风险；即使基于试验结果开展NDA前咨询，也担忧无法获得NDA批准。；1305-0052试验设计：N≈448，1:1随机，Nerandomilast 18mg bid vs 安慰剂，主要终点为至疾病进展或全因死亡时间，关键次要终点为第52周FVC变化和mRSS变化。；1305-0052主要终点（至疾病进展或死亡时间）在其他SSc关键试验中尚无先例作为主要终点使用。
decision: 本次PEC讨论性质为信息共享和征求建议，非背书请求。
todo: 准备HAI回复并纳入CTA提交包（owner/due/status：原文未说明）。；与全球ET保持密切沟通，就CTA补充支持性证据进行协调（owner/due/status：原文未说明）。；与全球ET和本地AT保持密切沟通，就未来NDA策略进行协调（owner/due/status：原文未说明）。
source_ref: PEC-Dec 2025/PEC-Dec 2025/10. China development strategy for Nerandomilast SSc indication__pre-reads for PEC Dec.pptx

chunk-cbde055a752d: The global strategy involves proceeding directly to a ph3 trial for the SSc indication without awaiting results from the ph2b CONQUEST trial, based on encouraging subgroup data for SSc-ILD from the FIBRONEER-ILD trial and supportive preclinical evidence.
China integration strategy for SSc project has been endorsed by CEC in Aug 2025.

Feedback from FDA, CDE and PMDA consistently highlighted that the current data is insufficient for a confirmatory ph3 trial in SSc. Risks for the final NDA approval of SSc indication were also raised.
RoFD for SSc was released by BUEC on Nov 18th and ph3 trial in SSc will be proceed.

CTA: CDE has not yet provided feedback regarding the specific study design and further review will be needed during CTA review; although the likelihood of CDE directly rejecting the CTA application is low, the approval letter may include remarks related to insufficient evidence and concerns.
    - EC: Concerns may be raised by site ECs due to unclear risk-benefit profile in SSc patients, which could potentially impact the subsequent trial execution.
    - NDA: remarks on the HAI feedback and CTA approval letter need to be addressed in NDA submission; approval of SSc indication may be challengi

China CTA submission strategy has been endorsed by CEC in Nov and aligned with global ET.
Risks associated with final NDA approval were communicated to local AT in Nov.
chunk-9c5f8fdbc859: FDA: The SSc-ILD subgroup data’s relevance to the broader SSc population remains uncertain; a ph 2 dose-finding/POC trial is recommended to guide ph3; conducting a ph3 trial based on available data is at your discretion.

CDE: current evidence is insufficient to justify proceeding directly to a pivotal trial for SSc; a dose-exploratory trial for SSc or provide additional evidence would support advancing to a pivotal trial for SSc.

PMDA: Interpreting the results may be difficult, and there is a high risk that a negative judgment may have to be made even if proposed primary endpoint meets; no intention to halt the conduct of the 1305-0052 trial due to no safety concerns; even if a pre-NDA consultation is conducted based on the trial’s findings, there is concern that it may not result in NDA approval.
chunk-c328e52771a3:
Primary Endpoint:
Time to the first occurrence of disease progression or all-cause death:
Adjudicated SSc-related clinically meaningful disease progression or complications*, or
Absolute decline in FVC% predicted ≥5%, or
Relative increase in mRSS ≥25% and absolute increase in mRSS ≥5 points, or
All-cause death
The primary endpoint proposed in the 1305-0052 trial has not been used as the primary endpoint in other pivotal trials for SSc.
